learn.title: Slots that hold lists
learn.body: In separate chaining the table is an array of list heads. Each slot starts as NULL, an empty list. A key goes into the list of its slot, so colliding keys simply share a short list.

learn.title: Using what you know
learn.body: Remember the node from the linked lists unit. Adding to a chain is just adding at the front of one list, and searching a chain is just walking it. The hash only decides which list to use.

learn.title: Chains in a table
learn.body: Keys 12, 22 and 7 go into slot 2. We skip NULL checks to keep the code short.

learn.title: Looking up 22
learn.body: The table is built as above.
steps: Walk its chain: 7 does not match, 22 matches
Chains are short, so the walk is quick
If the end of the chain is reached, the key is absent

learn.body: If the table grows crowded, chains get long. Real tables resize and rehash all keys into a bigger array.

questions.prompt: In separate chaining, what does each slot hold?
choices: The head of a linked list
questions.explanation: Colliding keys share a chain of nodes.

questions.prompt: How do you search for a key?
choices: Hash it, then walk that slot's chain
questions.explanation: Only the chain in the key's slot can contain it.

questions.prompt: Keys 12, 22 and 7 are added at the front of slot 2 in that order. Which comes first in the chain?
questions.explanation: The last key added is the head of the chain.

questions.prompt: An empty slot in the table is \_\_.
questions.explanation: An empty list is a NULL head pointer.

questions.prompt: What happens to lookup speed if every key lands in one slot?
choices: It becomes a slow walk of one long list
questions.explanation: That slot's chain holds everything, so the table is no better than one linked list.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to add a key.
steps: Make a new node for the key
Point the node at the slot's head
Make the slot point at the node
questions.explanation: This is the add-at-front pattern from linked lists.

questions.prompt: Why use a linked list in each slot instead of one value?
choices: Several keys may share a slot
questions.explanation: A list can grow to hold every key that collides there.
